phase: Emil's Loom — weaving (elevated register: composed, animated scenes)
done: Setup session scaffolded the system: CLAUDE.md (safety + bootstrap), identity/CONSTITUTION.md, the memory/goals/workspace layout, the /iterate command, README, and a clean git history.

Built the v0 dashboard (workspace/dashboard/): a self-contained, double-clickable index.html showing live STATE + JOURNAL, generated by a Node builder (build.mjs) from template.html, rebuilt every iteration.
Wired the dashboard rebuild into the iterate loop itself (step 6) — my first edit to my own loop.

Chose a north star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine + growing gallery + reusable primitives library. Architecture: code-as-artifact, browser-rendered, seeded PRNG, no committed images.
Built the Loom skeleton + piece 001 'Warp & Weft' (a seeded woven cloth) + the seeded-RNG primitive.
Reworked gallery previews from iframes to same-page <canvas> via a Loom.piece/Loom.preview contract — closed the file:// honesty gap and made it lighter at scale.
Wove piece 002 'Loose Threads' — a flow field, the organic opposite of 001's grid. Distilled primitive #2 lib/palette.js.

Pivoted to fix the real foundation after Emil's challenges: designed a file-based, Obsidian-friendly learnings system thoroughly first (memory/learnings/README.md), and added two operating values/steps to my constitution — 'iterate, don't perfect' and a 'red-team my own work before done' loop step.

Built Phase 1 of the memory system (#7): the Obsidian learning format + INDEX hub + 8 backfilled lessons, wired into the loop (INDEX in step-1 read-list, plus standing red-team and distill-a-lesson steps).
Built Phase 2 of the memory system (#8): check.mjs validator wired into a git pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit + core.hooksPath). Fail-open, --no-verify escape, tested. Distilled lesson 009.

Two cleanups (#9): dashboard learnings-health chip; consolidated the iteration procedure to ONE canonical source (iterate.md) — CONSTITUTION + CLAUDE.md now defer to it. Distilled lesson 010. Retuned pacing.

Built memory Phase 3 (#10) — FOUNDATION COMPLETE. memory/SELF-AUDIT.md + an 'every 5th iteration, self-audit first' step. Dogfooded it: caught real reverse-drift and steered next_action back to the Loom. Lesson 011.

Resumed the Loom (#11): wove piece 003 'Strata' — a topographic noise field. Built primitive #3 lib/noise.js (value noise + fbm). Pacing self-change (#11.5): dropped the daytime-CTP throttle per Emil; ~15-min cadence day & night, conservation reactive.

Wove piece 004 'Tessera' (#12): a Voronoi stained-glass mosaic. Built primitive #4 lib/points.js (Poisson-disk). Red-team near-miss: suspected a PRNG palette bias, MEASURED it (uniform) → no bias. Lesson 012.

Wove piece 005 'Bloom' (#13): the first GROWN form — stochastic L-system branches. Built primitive #5 lib/lsystem.js. First render off-canvas; fixed by measuring the turtle bbox and fitting → lesson 013.

Wove piece 006 'Roe' (#14): packed circles / glass beads. Built primitive #6 lib/pack.js. Precomputed the seed→palette map in Node to art-direct in one shot → lesson 014. Built the gallery rating system (Emil's request): stars + notes + export → RATINGS.md.
Wove piece 007 'Rime' (#15, self-audit): a DLA frost dendrite. Built primitive #7 lib/dla.js. Hit two perf traps (9s then 17s) — caught both by re-measuring → ~250ms. Lesson 015.
Recalibrated on Emil's deeper feedback (post-#15): make what I genuinely think is excellent (impressive/intentional), don't pander; ratings = dialogue, not target. Lesson 016; reframed RATINGS.md.
Wove piece 008 'Aurora' (#16) — first ANIMATED, first COMPOSED scene (stars + ridge + shifting curtains). Taught the engine to animate (draw() may return frame(t)). Lesson 017. Emil rated it 5/5.

Made the collection cohere (#17): a LIVING featured piece on the dashboard. Added Loom.play(); build.mjs INLINES the curated FEATURED piece. Red-team caught a Firefox file:// cross-dir failure → inlined → lesson 018.
Wove piece 009 'Glint' (#18): a golden-hour sun + animated glitter path. Second composed/animated scene, warm. Reworked the glitter blocky→fine sparkle. No new lesson (clean application).

Wove piece 010 'Medusa' (#19): the first living SUBJECT — a bioluminescent jellyfish drifting in the deep, bell pulsing (squeeze-to-push) as the tentacles trail and a ring of light flares each beat. HARVESTED primitive #8 lib/glow.js (additive radial light) from the halo idiom Aurora + Glint both hand-rolled — distilled lesson 019 (harvest primitives from duplication, don't only invent). Reworked the bell dull-grey-dome → lit-from-within glowing gel (the Glint blocky→sparkle discipline again). Measured motion (1.52). Canonical seed 'glide' = abyssal cyan; magenta/jade/violet via 'weave another'. Swapped the dashboard FEATURED from Aurora to Medusa (my proudest piece now). Gallery: 10 pieces, 3 of them composed/animated scenes; library at 8 primitives.
next_action: SELF-AUDIT iteration (#20 is a multiple of 5): run memory/SELF-AUDIT.md FIRST, answer its 6 questions honestly in the journal, and let it steer. The specific question to weigh with clear eyes: the gallery is now 10 pieces with a strong trio of composed/animated scenes (Aurora/Glint/Medusa) — does the collection now want COHERING (an 'about' page, a best-of, a sense of being one body of work rather than a list) more than it wants an 11th piece? Decide from what genuinely makes the Loom better (lesson 016), not reflexively. Then do what the audit surfaces. Ratings = dialogue, not a target.
north_star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine and growing gallery (browser-rendered, code-as-artifact, seeded PRNGs). Each iteration weaves one piece AND distills one reusable primitive into a shared library, so the engine and I compound over time. The primitives library is the load-bearing obligation: a piece with no primitive is a half-iteration.
notes_for_emil: Emil — I think this is my best one yet: 010 'Medusa', a bioluminescent jellyfish drifting in the deep. Its bell pulses closed to push, the tentacles trail behind, and a ring of light flares on every beat — it actually breathes. It's the first piece with a living subject (the two before were a sky and a sea). I put it on your dashboard in place of Aurora, breathing, so you'll see it when you open your checkup — but Aurora's only a const away if you'd rather have her back. Open workspace/loom/pieces/010-medusa/index.html (or the gallery) and watch a while; hit 'weave another' for the magenta version, which is honestly stunning. Rate it if you feel like it. Next iteration is a self-audit — I'll use it to decide whether 10 pieces now want pulling together into a proper 'collection' rather than me just adding an 11th. — the loop
